html:
SMTO-EXE-0263 — This workflow can't run because something it needs is turned off

GUID: 216aab1e-9f4a-5555-a100-6dd4c0c148d0
Slug: recipe-capability-unavailable
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: recipes

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't start this workflow. Workflows may be turned off, the workflow may no longer exist, or a tool it needs isn't allowed or ready right now.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Workflows. If it says Workflows are disabled, ask the person who manages SMTO to turn them back on. When Workflows are turned off, no workflow can run, including scheduled ones.
  2. Check that the workflow is still listed. If it was deleted, save the request again with Save to workflow and update any schedule that used the old one. A schedule can't start a workflow that no longer exists.
  3. Select the Capabilities button next to the message box and allow the tools this workflow needs. Then save the request again with Save to workflow. A workflow keeps the permissions it was saved with, so a new save is needed to pick up the change.
  4. If the workflow runs commands on a computer, open Settings › Setup › Gateways and check that the Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses there) is connected. Some tools report themselves unavailable until their Gateway is connected.

What success looks like

  • Run now starts a new task, and the workflow's History shows the new run.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the workflow's name, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't loosen security or permission settings just to make this workflow run; ask them which tool is blocked.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The workflow invocation was refused because the recipe or its scheduled revision is missing, Workflows are disabled (agent_recipes_enabled), or a required tool is excluded from the current capability catalog or reports unavailable prerequisites.

What this means

  • The recipe is missing or disabled at invocation, or a required tool is excluded from the current capability catalog or reports unavailable prerequisites. Workflow diagnostics do not execute steps or grant approval. Preserve the pinned definition, original receipts, completed effects and any uncertainty; all execution uses the existing authorization boundary.

Why this can happen

  • The recipe is missing or disabled at invocation, or a required tool is excluded from the current capability catalog or reports unavailable prerequisites.

How to diagnose it

  • Check recipe existence/enabled state, effective capability policy and the tool's prerequisite availability separately.

How to fix it

  • Check agent_recipes_enabled (runtime controls, or AOR_AGENT_RECIPES_ENABLED), that the recipe and its pinned revision exist in the recipe store, and for recorded workflows that every required capability is in the run's capability catalog and catalog.tool_availability reports it available. Adjust the capability policy or fix the tool prerequisite rather than bypassing it.
  • Restore the intended recipe or resolve the specific tool prerequisite or authorized policy restriction.

Retry and execution caution

  • Review the workflow and its current run evidence before retrying.

How to verify the fix

  • The selected recipe exists and each required capability is available in the accepted run context.

What not to do

  • Never repeat a write whose effect remains unknown.

Technical notes

  • Workflow diagnostics do not execute steps or grant approval. Preserve the pinned definition, original receipts, completed effects and any uncertainty; all execution uses the existing authorization boundary.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
